title: DeepBench: Savings Orchestration & Initiative Log
creator: Aisha Ramachandran
description: Objective: coordinate a cross-functional initiative (DeepBench) to orchestrate targeted savings across batching, KV prefix caching, and model quantization profiles for a set of medium-high volume routes. Scope: define per-route policy recommendations, roll out a safe field trial for a cohort of customers, and instrument a metric surface to quantify dollars saved and quality delta. Deliverables: (1) policy catalog + per-route heuristics, (2) trial runbook and rollback gates, (3) dashboards for unit cost and quality regressions, (4) code + infra tickets to implement safe rollout. Success metrics: >=12% average token-cost reduction on trial routes with <1.5% end-user quality regression (as measured by rubric and automated evals), clear per-route ROI signal, and automated rollback on regressions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Policy catalog committed to repo and reviewed by runtime + infra. 2) Field trial runbook published with clear SLOs and rollback thresholds. 3) Savings dashboard populated with per-route token cost baseline and trial cohort reports. 4) Two-round A/B trial completed with statistical significance tests and a decision recorded. 5) Post-trial playbook for org-wide rollouts.
comments: 2025-02-12 | Aisha Ramachandran: Created the initiative to centralize per-route savings controls. Attached initial PRD and a coarse risk matrix. Goal is to avoid ad-hoc one-off optimizations that are hard to maintain.

2025-02-20 | Lena Chen (PM): Aligned scope with runtime: start with 6 routes (search, summarize, chat-system, code-completion, labeler, rerank). Prioritize routes by token-volume * cost-per-token. Request ENG to propose safe quant profiles for two open LLM families.

2025-02-25 | Miguel Ortega (Eng): Kernel scheduling prototype shows ~8% baseline improvement when combined with adaptive batching; KV prefetch needs an API change to expose route-level TTLs. Filed ENG-4519 for prefetch TTL work.

2025-02-28 | Priya Nair (Research): Ran offline quality evals comparing int8 and q4_0 profiles on sample prompts. Average BLEU-like score shows 0.9% drop; flagged a subset of prompts for manual review. Added test harness to /internal/deepbench/evals.

2025-03-03 | Design Review (Ethan Park): UX for console policy page draft reviewed. Suggest showing projected $ savings per 1000 reqs and a clear checkbox for "auto-rollforward" vs "manual approval". Small copy edits suggested for rollback wording.

2025-03-04 | Lena Chen (PM): Kickoff retrospective scheduled after pilot completion. Action item: get runtime canary window set up and link to cost dashboard. ENG asked for two-week lead to implement route TTLs; moved trial start to 2025-03-18.
2025-03-04 | QA (Sofia Alvarez): Proposed gating tests: negative tests for degradations >2% and synthetic drift detection. Will create test matrix by 2025-03-10.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: quantization may introduce subtle quality regressions on edge-case prompts. Mitigation: two-stage rollout with automated evals + manual sampling, immediate auto-rollback if regression crosses threshold. Risk: inaccurate baseline leading to overstated savings. Mitigation: use 14-day rolling baseline with traffic stratification, surface confidence intervals on dashboard. Risk: infra changes (TTL API) might delay rollouts. Mitigation: implement a soft-traffic shim that approximates TTL behavior until infra change is deployed.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (Weeks 1-3): finalize policy catalog, infra tickets (ENG-4519), eval harness and dashboards. Phase 2 (Weeks 4-6): small closed cohort trial (n=5 customers), monitor quality and cost signals. Phase 3 (Week 7): analyze results, decision meeting: scale, iterate, or abort. Post-mortem and playbook (Week 8).
notes: - Coordinate with Customer Success for whitelist of customers suitable for closed-cohort trials. - Budget: allow up to $8k trial margin for unexpected reruns. - Ensure telemetry tags include 'deepbench_cohort' and 'policy_variant' for traceability.
